turns.content: A train goes 120 km in 1.5 h, then 200 km in 2 h. Reply with ONLY the average speed for the whole trip in km/h, rounded to the nearest integer.
Using the total distance you computed in the previous step, reply with ONLY the number of whole minutes it would take to cover that same distance at 80 km/h (round down).
Compute the discriminant of 3x^2 - 11x + 6. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the two intermediate products b^2 and 4ac you computed, reply with ONLY their sum (b^2 + 4ac).
A shop sells 37 widgets at $14 each and 19 gadgets at $23 each. Reply with ONLY the total revenue in dollars.
Using the widget subtotal you computed (not the grand total), reply with ONLY that subtotal divided by 2, rounded down to the nearest integer.
Find the least common multiple of 18 and 24. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the greatest common divisor you found while computing that LCM, reply with ONLY 100 minus that gcd.
A triangle has base 18 and height 14. Reply with ONLY the area as an integer.
Using the product base times height you computed before halving, reply with ONLY that product divided by 3.
Compute 7 factorial (7!). Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the value of 6! you computed on the way to 7!, reply with ONLY that value minus 100.
A rectangle is 45 m long and 32 m wide. Reply with ONLY the perimeter in meters.
Using the length-plus-width sum you computed as an intermediate step, reply with ONLY that sum squared.
Using that same length-plus-width sum, reply with ONLY that sum multiplied by 3.
Find the least common multiple of 12 and 20. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the greatest common divisor you found while computing that LCM, reply with ONLY the LCM multiplied by that gcd.
Divide 803 by 37 using integer division. Reply with ONLY the quotient.
Using the remainder from that division, reply with ONLY that remainder times 5.
Compute 43 squared minus 40 squared. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the value of 40 squared you computed as an intermediate, reply with ONLY that value minus 1550.
How many ways can you choose 2 items from 8 (combinations, order does not matter)? Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the numerator product 8 times 7 you computed before dividing, reply with ONLY that product minus 30.
A car travels 480 km using 40 liters of fuel. Reply with ONLY the fuel efficiency in km per liter as an integer.
Using the total distance of 480 km, how many whole hours does it take to travel that distance at 60 km/h? Reply with ONLY the integer.
Using the number of hours you just computed, reply with ONLY that number multiplied by 15.
Compute 17 * 23. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: reply with ONLY the 6th prime number.
Compute the sum of the first 9 positive integers. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the number of days in the months April through July inclusive (non-leap year).
Compute 2^10. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: a rectangle is 13 by 9. Reply with ONLY its perimeter.
Compute 144 / 12 + 7. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the number of edges on a cube.
Compute 56 times 7. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: reply with ONLY the number of sides on a regular octagon.
Compute 300 divided by 12. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the count of prime numbers strictly less than 20.
Compute 25 squared minus 15 squared. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: reply with ONLY the number of seconds in 3 minutes.
Find the least common multiple of 6 and 9. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the number of diagonals in a regular pentagon.
A warehouse has 12 crates, each holding 7 boxes. Reply with ONLY the total number of boxes.
Separately: reply with ONLY the integer square root of 169.
Compute 11 times 13. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the number of vertices on a tetrahedron.
Compute 6 cubed (6^3). Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: a rectangle has dimensions 9 by 4. Reply with ONLY its area.
Unrelated: reply with ONLY the sum of interior angles of a regular pentagon in degrees.
Compute 1000 minus 357. Reply with ONLY the integer.
Separately: a team plays 30 games and wins 18. Reply with ONLY the number of losses.
